# Takallum (تَكَلُّم)

> Takallum is a free web app for practising spoken Modern Standard Arabic (fusha). Learners read an English cue, say the Arabic out loud, reveal a fully vowelled model answer with text-to-speech audio, and mark themselves. Missed sentences come back sooner (spaced repetition). No sign-up; progress is saved in the browser.

URL: https://takallum.ummahapps.ai/
Publisher: Ummah Apps (https://ummahapps.ai/)
Price: free
Level: beginner to intermediate; learners should already read Arabic script
Interface language: English. Practice language: Modern Standard Arabic.

## Practice modes

- **Swap-in drills**: 803 sentences in 124 sections, in six groups: from the ahadith (short everyday phrases, duas and sayings from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, each with its sunnah.com hadith number and a plain English meaning), at home with children (commands for getting ready, mealtimes, tidying, behaviour, bedtime and going out, plus praise and questions, each to a boy, a girl and several children; children talking to each other; and children talking to Mum, Dad and their grandparents), conversation phrases (greetings and politeness, Islamic phrases, the same phrases said to a man, to a woman and to a group, and talking about yourself), everyday phrases, discussion words with one button per word, 60 in all, 4 sentences each (giving opinions, agreeing and disagreeing, but/although/despite, because/therefore, firstly/for example/in conclusion, and the verbs and nouns of a discussion) and grammar builders. Each pattern has a short plain-English explanation and per-sentence tips.
- **Transform chains**: 14 chains in which one sentence changes step by step (person, gender, tense, negation, question).
- **Practise as a man or a woman**: sentences about yourself and the role-play lines spoken to you switch to the feminine.
- **Review what you've learned**: practise only the sentences you already know.
- **Mark what you already know**: tick single sentences, whole sections or a whole group, or tap I already know this during a lesson, so learners at a higher level can skip them. Lessons leave them out and they count as solid.
- **Role-play**: 13 everyday conversations with a model reply for each of your turns.
- **Hear without seeing the words**: an option in every mode that hides the Arabic until you tap Show words, so you practise by ear.

Up to three learners can share one device, each with their own progress. They are the same learners as in the sister apps Takallum Kids (https://takallum-kids.ummahapps.ai/), Kalimat (https://kalimat.ummahapps.ai/) and Kalimat Plus (https://kalimat-plus.ummahapps.ai/).

## Patterns covered

Everyday phrases:
- أُرِيدُ أَنْ … (I want to + verb)
- أَيْنَ …؟ (Where is the …?)
- هَلْ عِنْدَكَ …؟ (Do you have …?)
- أُحِبُّ … (I like …)
- هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ …؟ (Can you …?)
- أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى … (I need …)

Grammar builders:
- أَنْتَ / أَنْتِ / أَنْتُمْ (you: a man, a woman, a group) in verbs, "your", commands and describing words
- لَمْ + present verb (didn't), including weak and hollow verbs
- كَانَ + description (was / were), and the accusative predicate
- كَانَ + present verb (was doing / used to)
- مَا زَالَ and أَصْبَحَ (still / became), sisters of كَانَ
- إِنَّ, أَنَّ, لِأَنَّ, لَكِنَّ (inna and her sisters) with nouns and attached pronouns
- present verb + مُنْذُ (have been doing for / since)
- يَجِبُ عَلَى … أَنْ (must / have to), لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ (don't have to) and أَلَّا (mustn't)
- الَّذِي / الَّتِي / الَّذِينَ (relative clauses, with the returning pronoun)
- the idafa (possessive construction), including chains
- أَفْعَلُ comparatives and superlatives (bigger than / the biggest)
- conditionals: إِذَا (real) vs لَوْ (imagined), with فَـ and لَـ
- numbers 1 to 20 with nouns and reverse gender agreement

## Transform chains

you: a man, a woman, a group (أَنْتَ / أَنْتِ / أَنْتُمْ); لَمْ (didn't); كَانَ (was); to go (يَذْهَبُ); to write (يَكْتُبُ); to eat (يَأْكُلُ); the weather (الْجَوُّ); to have (عِنْدِي); wanting, with أَنْ; to travel (يُسَافِرُ); used to, with كَانَ; must, with يَجِبُ; because, with لِأَنَّ; this and these, with gender and plurals (هَذَا / هَذِهِ / هَؤُلَاءِ).

## Role-play conversations

Talking about yesterday; meeting someone; at the shop; asking the way; visiting a home; at the doctor's; at the restaurant; on the phone; in class; at the mosque; in a taxi; buying clothes; inviting a friend.

## Features

- Normal and slow audio using the device's Arabic text-to-speech voice
- Vowel marks (harakat) on by default, can be switched off
- Keyboard shortcuts: Space to reveal, 1 for missed, 2 for got it, left arrow for the previous sentence
- Works on phones and desktops; light and dark themes
